Food service as % of Pepsi revenue
Convenience foot traffic decline (7-Eleven et al.)
High 40s to 50%; Q3 impacted 'even greater than anticipated'

Management reframed a difficult intra-quarter narrative around long-term positioning: #3 player in a ~$28B energy category, growing ~10x category rate, driving ~40-47% of category growth on three megatrends (better-for-you, function, fitness lifestyle).

Most material disclosure: Pepsi inventory-optimization drag escalated to ~$100-120M of reduced Q3 orders vs PY (after ~$47M in H1); revenue is recognized on delivery to Pepsi, not on sell-through, creating a 'disconnect' vs strong scanner data.
Management warned the Pepsi order reduction would hit Q3 gross margins 'even greater than we anticipated'; stressed the optimization is 'out of our control.'

Management firmly rejected the interpretation that Pepsi's pullback signals macro caution; attributed it solely to 'supply chain optimization on their side' (Pepsi held several million more cases than needed).
Energy category sharply slowing amid macro pressure on mid/low-income consumers; some top players posted negative growth 'for the first time in a generation'; convenience foot traffic down ~4%.

Management argued the category is NOT losing consumers to other categories - it is a frequency/intensification reduction, not category abandonment - so Celsius is positioned to capture returning consumers.
Large shelf-space gains: ~35% MULOC, ~43-45% convenience, ~39-45% TDP YoY; management acknowledged large space gains historically cause a temporary per-point velocity dip while new space fills out.
Switched share reporting to Circana MULO+ with convenience (~11.8% share) to better capture omnichannel (Amazon, .com, club); Amazon ~10% of Q2 sales, club ~22%.
Food service is a major opportunity: >12% of revenue through Pepsi; in Jersey Mike's, testing at Pizza Hut; expands the energy usage occasion (breakfast, lunch, pre-workout).
2024 pricing actions followed top players; front-line pricing 'expands the toolbox'; no material 2024 impact, price 'dealt back' via promotions in 2024, benefit deferred to 2025.
International only ~5% of revenue mix vs ~40% for Monster - a structural growth runway; Suntory-partnered Phase 1 markets: UK/Ireland launched, France/Australia/New Zealand/Benelux ahead.

Marketing slate: Charles Leclerc/Ferrari F1, MLS initiative, Breakaway music festival, Live Fit Tour, Celsius U Ambassador Program (120 grads/80+ universities), Jake Paul-Mike Tyson Netflix event sponsorship.

Catalysts: NACS show (Oct 2024) as 'next big opportunity'; 2025 retailer space negotiations 'very positive'; expected category/convenience-traffic recovery; Monster expected to begin taking price in Q4.
Catch up newcomers on where Celsius plays in energy and how it turned the category into a three-way race.

Fieldly: #3 player in ~$28B category with growth runway, differentiated on three megatrends (better-for-you with 7+ vitamins/green tea/ginger/guarana; clinically-proven functional energy backed by 6+ peer-reviewed studies; fitness 'Live Fit' lifestyle); achieved 10 share (first in a decade), grows ~10x category, leverages PepsiCo North America distribution partnership and Suntory international (UK/Ireland launched).
How is Celsius faring more than halfway through an unseasonably challenging Q3 for the energy category?

David: macro-challenged consumer hitting the category for the first time in some time; some top players posting negative growth; Celsius resilient at +10% QTD YoY (~10x category), ~45% convenience space gains; large TDP gains (+39-45%) historically produce a temporary velocity dip. Fieldly: bullish on H2 and 2025; sugar-free now 50% of category sales, Celsius clear #2.
Q2 call flagged a $20-30M revenue headwind from Pepsi reducing inventory - more detail and is more impact expected in Q3?

Fieldly: scanner sales +~10% QTD, depletions tracking similarly; H1 2024 saw ~$47M of reduced orders from Pepsi optimizing inventory, escalating in Q3 to a YTD estimate of ~$100-120M reduced orders; revenue recognized on delivery to Pepsi creates a 'disconnect' he called unfortunate/disappointing. David: ~$100-120M less Q3 orders vs PY, Pepsi held several million more cases than needed and is now optimizing.
Confirm the Pepsi impact relates to optimization in a new relationship - and do conversations suggest Pepsi macro concern (Frito-Lay impacts, lower-income consumer)?

Fieldly firmly rejected macro caution: 'really supply chain optimization on their side'; Celsius is the growth driver (47% of category growth), a leading brand in Pepsi's portfolio; recent AOP meeting produced 2025 strategies; implemented an incentive program with Pepsi to align expectations and unlock display inventory and priority periods.
What levers is Celsius pulling to keep pushing the market-share growth story?

Fieldly: marketing/partnership slate - Charles Leclerc/Ferrari F1, MLS initiative, new Breakaway music-festival partnership (Essential Vibes Tour), Live Fit Tour (5Ks/workouts), and Celsius U Ambassador Program (120 grads, 80+ universities, NIL partnerships) - all bringing new consumers and growing the category.
Shelf-space gains across channels & timing of payoff
Have space gains been similar across channels, and how should timing of the payoff be modeled?

David: total MULOC space +~35%, convenience +~43%; convenience is the key future growth driver (~65% of Red Bull/Monster sales, key for trial - 'when we get trial, we know it sticks'); category not losing consumers, just frequency reduction; 2025 retailer meetings 'very positive.' Fieldly: NACS in October is the next big opportunity; pursuing additional space, better placements, cold checkout placements.
Management's direct view on what is driving the category slowdown, and is it comparable across the three brands?

Fieldly: mid/low-income consumers being affected, visible in convenience data; Celsius led category growth (40% of growth); consumers are not moving to other categories - it is reduced frequency due to the economic climate; confident in recovery and Celsius well positioned, especially as the sugar-free movement becomes the category driver.
Explain the new Circana MULO+ with convenience measure and why it better tracks Celsius's trend.

Fieldly: MULO+ captures the omnichannel world (Amazon, target.com, walmart.com, club); Celsius over-indexes on Amazon (#1/#2 in energy) and club; measure shows ~11.8% share. David: Amazon and Costco are among the largest US retailers (Amazon ~10% of Q2 sales, club ~22%), so excluding them makes no sense - the measure is more representative.
Greater opportunity in one channel vs another, and do channels rise/fall in importance under macro pressure?

David: variety of pack-size/channel strategies; value multipacks perform extremely well but management is cautious if the basket ring becomes too large under consumer pressure; food service is a major opportunity (>12% of revenue through Pepsi - hospitals, universities, Lowe's, restaurants; in Jersey Mike's, testing Pizza Hut), expanding the energy usage occasion.
Have the H2 promotions started, and how long will the investment last (per the Q2 high-40s-to-50% margin commentary)?

Fieldly: category highly promotional (~26 weeks/year avg); Celsius leaning into promotions in the post-reset quarter; strong Q2 gross profit and efficiency gains, more supply-chain efficiencies planned for 2025; warned the ~$100-120M Q3 Pepsi order reduction will impact Q3 margins 'even greater than we anticipated.'
Is the slated promotional activity and in-market execution still on track?
Fieldly: on track, nothing outside the ordinary - additional promotions and targeted retail marketing programs; the perfect time to lean in with retailers ahead of back-half buyer reviews.
How to think about pricing approach; and skeptics say it is 'an odd time to raise prices' amid a macro-pressured consumer - broader view on industry-wide pricing?

Fieldly: strong pricing architecture, Celsius warrants a premium position; followed top players in taking price but no upside realized in H2 2024 - transpires into 2025+; front-line pricing 'expands the toolbox' (EDLP, high-low, bundling); no material 2024 impact. David: will 'deal back' the price via promotions in 2024; Monster 'supposedly' begins taking price in Q4 and has been aggressive with BOGOs, whereas Celsius rarely runs BOGOs.
Strategy and ramp timing for the new Suntory international markets, and long-term international mix potential?

Fieldly: international ~5% of revenue mix vs ~40% for Monster - a massive opportunity; health/wellness trends are global; UK/Australia study showed higher-than-expected brand awareness; launched in UK and Ireland with Suntory (into Tesco), entering gyms first with a methodical approach; Phase 1 markets: UK, Ireland, France (later 2024), Australia, New Zealand, Benelux; more markets in 2025-2026.
How does Celsius build awareness internationally given it enters gyms first?

Fieldly: a 'drill-deep' playbook built in the US (Boston a top market, well above a 15 share) builds awareness, trial, acceptance and loyalty, executed successfully in Sweden and Finland; measured, ROI-focused approach (not a land-grab); tied to global-reach bets - Ferrari F1 with Charles Leclerc and the Jake Paul-Mike Tyson fight, where Celsius is a major sponsor of Netflix's first live national sporting event.
